Sībawayh related that he heard some crude Arabs read: "wa lam yakun aḥadun kufuwan lahu," and this boor followed his habit, his nature being unrefined regarding the subtle meaning that required placing the adverbial phrase with the predicate before the noun. The purpose for which the verse was brought is the negation of equality and parity from the Essence of God, exalted is He. So placing the equality intended to be negated first was more fitting; then, since it was placed first to be negated, the adverbial phrase was mentioned with it to clarify the sacred Essence by negating equality. And God knows best.], so why is it placed first in the most eloquent and most correct speech? I say: this speech was brought only to negate equality from the Essence of the Creator, glory be to Him, and the focus and center of this meaning is this adverbial phrase, so it is the most important and most pertinent thing, and most deserving of being placed first and most fitting. It was read: "kufuwan," with damma on the kāf and the fāʾ, and with damma on the kāf and kasra with the fāʾ sukūn. If you ask: why is this sūra equal to the whole Qur'an, despite its brevity of text and closeness of its two ends? I say: for a matter that makes some people noble. And that is due only to its containing the attributes of God, His justice and His oneness. Sufficient as evidence is the one who acknowledges its excellence and believes the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) concerning it: "Indeed, the science of tawḥīd has a high station with God." And how could it not be so, when knowledge follows the known: it is honored by its honor and lowered by its lowliness; and the known of this science is God and His attributes, and what is permissible for Him and what is not. So what do you think of the nobility of its rank and the greatness of its station, and its superiority over every science, and its seizing the prize of precedence over it? Whoever scorns it does so from weakness of knowledge of its object, little reverence for it, emptiness of fear of it, and distance from contemplating its outcome. O God, gather us among those who know You and act for You, who affirm Your justice and Your oneness, who fear Your threat.

It is called Sūrat al-Asās (the Foundation Sūra) because it includes the foundations of religion. Ubayy and Anas related from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The seven heavens and the seven earths were founded upon Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad" [I have not found it as a marfūʿ report; Ibn Abī Shayba related it in Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān from the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Ghaylān al-Thaqafī from al-ʿAbb al-Aḥbār as a mawqūf report], meaning: they were created only to be signs of God's oneness and the knowledge of His attributes which this sūra expresses. It is related from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he heard a man recite "Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad" and said: "It is required (wajabat)." It was said: "O Messenger of God, what is required?" He said: "The Garden is required for him" [related by al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and al-Ḥākim from the hadith of ʿUbayd ibn Ḥunayn from Abū Hurayra. It has a witness in al-Ṭabarānī's al-Kabīr from the hadith of Abū Umāma].
